title: Refinishing Hardwood Floors in Seattle Condos: Rules, Noise, Elevators and Timing
meta: Refinishing hardwood in a Seattle condo costs the same $3.99 per sq ft as a house; the catch is HOA approval, quiet hours and elevators. From Wills Flooring.
keywords: refinish hardwood floors condo Seattle, condo floor refinishing HOA rules, refinishing floors in an apartment building, hardwood refinishing quiet hours elevator, Seattle condo floor sanding

blocks.lead: Yes, you can refinish hardwood in a Seattle condo, and it costs the same $3.99 per sq ft natural or $6.50 stained as a house; what changes is the logistics: written HOA approval, work inside quiet hours, an elevator reservation, dust and fume control for the neighbors, and a schedule built around cure time you cannot rush.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring refinishes condo floors from Belltown to Capitol Hill to Ballard every month. The 500 sq ft minimum applies, so a 450 sq ft unit is billed at 500. Low-odor, fast-drying water-based Bona finish is what makes it workable in a building full of neighbors.

blocks.html: Seattle condo floors fall into two families. The 1900s to 1920s brick and timber conversions in Pioneer Square, Belltown and lower Queen Anne have thick original fir or oak that sands like any house floor. The 1990s to 2010s mid-rises on Capitol Hill, in Ballard and around South Lake Union have engineered planks with a thin veneer that may or may not take a sanding. Both share a building manager, a rules document, an elevator and a downstairs neighbor. Here are the rules, the floor check, the schedule and the honest cases where a condo floor should be recoated or replaced instead.

blocks.text: The rules your building will enforce

items.title: Written approval and insurance
items.text: Most Seattle HOAs require a work request even for refinishing, plus the contractor's license and certificate of insurance. We supply ours the same day you ask. Allow one board cycle, often two to four weeks.

items.title: Quiet hours
items.text: Typical rules allow noisy work 8 or 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays. Sanding is the loud part and happens on days one and two; coating days are nearly silent, which helps when the window is tight.

items.title: Elevator and loading
items.text: Sanders, vacuums and finish come up a reserved freight or padded elevator. Belltown and Capitol Hill buildings often need a loading zone permit or a dock slot, which we arrange with the manager.

items.title: Sound rules do not change
items.text: Refinishing replaces the finish only. The floor assembly and any acoustic underlayment stay as they were, so the IIC rating your HOA cares about is unaffected. Say so on the request form.

items.text: Submit the work request with our license and insurance. Reserve the elevator for day one and the final day. Post a notice for the neighbors above, below and beside.
items.note: Boards that meet monthly are the usual delay.

items.text: Doorways sealed, air scrubber running, vacuum-connected sanders on the main area. This is the loud day, kept inside quiet hours.

blocks.text: When refinishing a condo floor is the wrong call

items: The veneer is under 2 mm. Sanding exposes plywood at the bevels and the floor is ruined. Recoat, or replace.
The finish is wax or a hardwax oil. Water-based polyurethane will not bond over it, so a recoat is off the table and a full sand is the only refinish option.
There is moisture from below. A slab-on-grade unit or a leak from a neighbor's line shows as cupping or dark edges. Fix the source first or the new finish fails the same way.
The HOA requires carpet coverage in bedrooms. Refinishing the living area still makes sense; refinishing under mandatory carpet does not.

The unit has 300 sq ft of exposed wood. The 500 sq ft minimum makes it $1,995 at the natural rate; sometimes a recoat at the same minimum is the better use of money. See what the minimum means for a small space.

blocks.title: Parking and loading in Seattle:
blocks.text: Capitol Hill, Belltown and Queen Anne are restricted parking zones, and our van has to sit somewhere for four days. We handle the loading zone permit or dock scheduling with your manager; the building's own fees, if any, are yours. Tell us the building's rules at the estimate.
Checklist for a smooth condo refinish

items.html: Find the flooring and alteration sections of your rules. Hours, insurance limits, elevator policy and notice requirements are all there. Send them to us before the estimate.
Know your wear layer. We measure it, but the building's original spec sheet, if the manager has it, settles the question fastest.
Book around the board meeting. Get the estimate first so the request packet is complete when the board sits.
Take the dust containment. In a shared building the $250 is cheap insurance against a complaint: doorways sealed, air scrubber running, on top of the vacuum-connected sanders.
Plan where you will sleep. Two to four nights away is normal. The unit is a work site until the last coat.
Use a crew that has done buildings before. Wills Flooring is licensed, insured, Bona Certified and backs the work with a 1-year workmanship warranty. Our refinishing page has the full process.

faq.q: Do I need HOA approval to refinish hardwood floors in a Seattle condo?
faq.a: Almost always. Most Seattle buildings treat refinishing as an alteration requiring a work request, the contractor's license and insurance, and agreed dates. Some allow a manager sign-off instead of a board vote. Check your rules; approval can take two to four weeks.

faq.q: How much does it cost to refinish condo floors in Seattle?
faq.a: The same as a house: $3.99 per sq ft natural, $6.50 with stain, $1.99 for a screen and recoat, with a 500 sq ft minimum. Dust containment is +$250. A 700 sq ft Capitol Hill unit, natural finish with containment, is 700 × $3.99 + $250 = $3,043.

faq.q: How loud is floor sanding for the neighbors?
faq.a: The sanding days are loud, similar to a vacuum cleaner running for hours, and travel through the structure. Coating days are almost silent. We keep all sanding inside the building's permitted hours and give you a notice to share with adjacent units.

faq.q: Can engineered floors in a newer condo be refinished?
faq.a: If the wear layer is 2 mm or more, usually once. Under 2 mm, no; a screen and recoat is the only option. We check the thickness at a register or closet edge before quoting, so you never pay for a sanding the floor cannot take.

faq.q: How long do I have to stay out of my condo?
faq.a: Most owners stay elsewhere for two to four nights. The floor is walkable in socks 24 hours after the final coat, furniture returns after 72 hours, and the finish fully cures over two to four weeks. Water-based finish makes this much shorter than oil-based.

faq.q: Does refinishing affect my condo's sound rating?
faq.a: No. Refinishing changes only the finish on top of the boards. The underlayment, subfloor and any acoustic mat stay untouched, so the IIC rating is the same after as before. Replacing the floor would raise the question; refinishing does not.
